_about: Script-VM opcode table: the single source for mnemonics, prototypes and descriptions (opcode_meta applies it over its built-in text). Reviewed 2026-09-27 against RF4S.exe and the shipped rf3.mc; set human_verified to true once a person has checked a row.

0.description: No-op: this dispatch slot is the shared do-nothing stub, so the VM decodes and discards any args and moves on.
0.details: RF4S.exe+0x193B0 is a bare `return 0` shared by 20 slots (ICF-folded; the IDB label BusInstance_SoLoud__vslot_002 is a linker artifact, not audio code). Args are popped by the VM as usual and ignored.
0.notes: Op 0 is never emitted in the shipped rf3.mc corpus of this review (0 uses).

1.description: Sets or clears bit 3 of the scene context's control word from bit 0 of the argument. Unused by the shipped scripts; its gameplay effect was not traced.
1.details: host+120 = (host+120 & ~8) | ((arg0 & 1) << 3). Needs argc >= 1, no kind check, never blocks, returns 0. Only bit 0 of the value matters.
1.notes: Behaviour is certain; the reader of host+120 bit 3 was not traced, so the name stays technical.

args.name: duration
args.notes: Must be a kind-0 (computed) value; the compiler always emits it that way.

tests.observed: the scene waits about 1 s

2.blocking: yes: for arg0/200 frames (at least one frame when 0 < arg0)
2.description: Pauses the script for a time. 12000 units = 1 second (200 per frame), so 6000 = half a second and Wait(1) yields exactly one frame.
2.details: Calls Quest_OnReactionDispatched_AdvanceState(host, 0) first (a one-shot latch that puts the player into the scripted-talk idle on the first call of a scene). Then requires argc == 1 and kind(arg0) == 0; if value != 0 and vm+112 == 4 (running) it sets vm+120 = value and vm+112 = 2 (waiting). The per-frame tick subtracts 200 from vm+120. Value 0, wrong argc or a non-zero kind make it a zero-length no-op.
2.side_effects: first call per scene freezes the player into the scripted-talk idle (Quest_OnReactionDispatched_AdvanceState latch)
2.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x1FAB50: `if (argc == 1 && !kind0 && v && vm->state == 4) { vm+120 = v; vm+112 = 2; }`; callee Quest_OnReactionDispatched_AdvanceState (+0x1EFA60); corpus: 5631 uses, top values 6000/18000/3000/12000 = 0.5/1.5/0.25/1 s, 199x Wait(1). In-game test 2026-09-29 (user): Wait(12000) freezes the scene for about 1 s (200 units per frame).

args.name: duration
args.notes: must be kind 0 and argc exactly 1, else no wait (the op still does its reset part)

3.blocking: yes: for the given duration (state 4 -> 2 with counter vm+120)
3.description: Like Wait, but first marks the scene controller as out of dialogue (the same idle write EndDialogue does, without closing the portraits), then waits the given time. Authors use it right before fades/warps after a talk.
3.details: RF4S.exe+0x1FAC20: host+872 -> +24 -> +116 = 1 (EndDialogue +0x203130 makes the same write; EmotePortrait_ShowFromDescriptor writes 2 when a portrait appears). Then Quest_OnReactionDispatched_AdvanceState(host, 0) (+0x1EFA60, runs once per latch host+116 bit 0x8000: drops the player's reaction task, Player_BeginScriptedTalkAndIdle, stops voice ids 0x1002248/0x1002249). Because +116 was just set to 1, that function takes the not-in-dialogue branch (v8 = 1, skips the +1604 resets) unless the controller +112 == 2. Then the op 2 wait: argc == 1, kind 0, value != 0 and vm+112 == 4 -> vm+120 = value, vm+112 = 2.
3.side_effects: scene controller dialogue state = 1; one-shot reaction-state advance (host+116 |= 0x8000)
3.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x1FAC20 vs op 2 +0x1FAB50 (identical except the +116 = 1 write); corpus: 77 uses, always 1 literal arg, 56x value 1, others 3000-30000.
3.notes: Name kept: 'reset' = the scene talk state reset. If a clearer name is wanted: EndTalkStateAndWait.

4.blocking: yes: for <duration> wait units (VM waiting state)
4.description: Pause the script for the given time, like Wait but without advancing the quest-reaction state. Authors use WaitPlain(1) to yield a single frame right after spawning actors.
4.details: Requires exactly argc == 1 and kind 0; a non-zero value while the VM is running (vm+112 == 4) sets vm+120 = duration and vm+112 = 2 (waiting). Always returns 0 - the wait is done by the VM state, not by re-running the op. 0 or a wrong argc does nothing.
4.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x1FABC0: `if (v2 >= 2*v4+1 && v4 == 1 && !kind0) { if (val && vm+112 == 4) { vm+120 = val; vm+112 = 2; } } return 0`; corpus: 12 uses, all WaitPlain(1) right after SpawnEventActor.
4.notes: Same body as op 2 (Wait) minus the Quest_OnReactionDispatched_AdvanceState call.

5.blocking: yes: while a screen fade task lacks its ready bit, or while the previous portrait in that slot is leaving / a modal scripted event holds bubbles
5.description: Show or change a character's E-mote portrait on the left or right side without touching the name plate, text blip, voice or emote icons. A DIALOG line must come after it (usually after the SetSpeaker… that names the speaker): the portrait belongs to the next line shown.
5.details: RF4S.exe+0x2077E0: returns 1 if g_currentFadeTask work+60 bit 2 is clear; descriptor {+8 = arg0, +10 = arg1, +12 = 0, +14 = arg2 (byte)} -> EmotePortrait_ShowFromDescriptor (+0x207370), whose return value is the op's. Side byte non-zero picks slot v1[24] and new portraits spawn at x 464; flip bit v1[29] 0x80000 = side & 1. Missing args read as an uninitialised local.
5.side_effects: spawns/updates a portrait task; scene controller +116 = 2
5.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x2077E0, +0x207370; corpus: 110 uses, argc 3, arg0 tag3 (actor), arg1 faces 0-69/255, arg2 0/1 (54/55) and one 254. Verified in game 2026-09-28 (user): needs a DIALOG after it. Corpus: 108 of 111 uses reach a DIALOG before the scene ends; the other 3 hand off through CALL / RET.

6.blocking: one frame or more: busy while a screen fade is running or while the slot's previous portrait is leaving
6.description: Show or update a character's E-mote speaker portrait on one side of the dialogue box, with an optional emote icon or voice clip. Does not change the name plate or the text blip, so it is used to change a listener's face between lines.
6.details: Builds a portrait descriptor {+8 char id = arg0, +10 expression = arg2, +14 side = arg1, +12 = arg3 when < 0x1F0} and calls EmotePortrait_ShowFromDescriptor (+0x207370): refreshes the portrait already in that side's slot if it shows the same character (EmotePortrait_Show), otherwise spawns a new one (EmotePortrait_SpawnPositioned). arg3 >= 0x1F0 goes to Sfx_PlayByIdWithNpcVariantRemap (+0x1FEDD0) and is not stored. Returns busy while the current fade task has not finished (work+60 bit 2 clear), and the dispatcher returns busy while a different character's portrait in the slot is still leaving or a modal scripted event holds the box.
6.side_effects: creates/updates a portrait task in host+88/+96; may play a sound
6.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x207900: descriptor build + `if (arg3 >= 0x1F0) Sfx_PlayByIdWithNpcVariantRemap(arg3); else BYTE4(desc)=arg3`; RF4S.exe+0x207370 slot select (side 0 -> host+88, side 1 -> host+96); corpus 1042 uses, always argc 4: arg0 char id / tag3, arg1 0/1, arg2 0..78 (op 6) or 1000..1926 (op 7), arg3 mostly 0, 186/188/191, or sfx ids 1677xxxx.
6.notes: Op 6 is used with tag3 character ids and low face indices, op 7 with literal ids and raw 1000+ entries; same code.

args.values: 0 = hide the name label, non-zero = show it

11.description: Hides (0) or shows (non-zero) the speaker-name label for the following DIALOG lines. Authors wrap sound-effect lines such as "*MUNCH*" in SetSpeakerNameVisible(0) ... SetSpeakerNameVisible(1).
11.details: Writes the dialogue flags dword g_gameGlobalsSlotTable.entries[4] bit 0 = (arg0 == 0) (bit set = name hidden). DialogueBox_SpawnBubbleAndSpeakerNameSprites and the line/text loaders copy that bit into the name sprite's hidden flag. Dialogue_LoadAndShowText (used by the SetSpeaker* cues) clears the bit on every load and sets it only for name id 0xFFFF, so a later speaker cue shows the name again.
11.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x20A4F0: `entries[4] = entries[4] & ~1 | (arg0 == 0)`; corpus: 1428 uses, values 0 (804) / 1 (624), pairs around '*MUNCH*', '*SQUEEZE*', '*GURGLE*' lines.

16.prototype: SetSpeaker(character, side, face, trigger1, trigger2, trigger3)

args.name: face
args.values: < 1000 = the character's face index (via g_emotePortrait_emoteToStringIdTable); 1000-1927 = raw expression entry (id-1000); 255 / 254 = the stock alternate expressions of the current outfit row (g_emotePortraitKindRows)

tests.observed: the MC's portrait on the left with a happy face

args.name: trigger1
args.values: 0 = none; 186-192 = emote icon over the portrait; >= 0x1F0 (in practice 0x1000000+n) = voice/sfx played via Sfx_PlayByIdWithNpcVariantRemap

args.name: trigger3
args.notes: optional; argc is clamped to 4; only the first two non-voice ids are kept

16.blocking: yes: while a screen fade task is active without its ready bit (g_currentFadeTask work+60 bit 2), and while the previous portrait on that side is still leaving / a modal scripted event holds the bubble (EmotePortrait_ShowFromDescriptor returns 1) (the fade wait is verified in game)
16.description: Speaker cue for the following DIALOG line(s): the player (Lest/Frey) speaks, portrait on the left side. Shows the E-mote portrait with the given face, sets the name plate and text blip when the speaker changes, and optionally plays a voice clip or pops an emote icon. Carries no text; stays in effect until the next speaker op or EndDialogue.
16.details: RF4S.exe+0x207F70: slot = (opcode-16)>>1 = 0, side = opcode & 1 = 0. Descriptor {+8 slot, +10 face, +12/+13 first two non-voice triggers, +14 side} -> EmotePortrait_ShowFromDescriptor (+0x207370): side picks portrait slot v1[22]/v1[24] and sets flip bit 0x80000 in v1[29]; a new portrait spawns via EmotePortrait_SpawnPositioned (+0x1D8110) at x -64 (side 0) or 464 (side 1). Blip: Dialogue_PickChimeClassForSpeaker (+0x1EF040) -> sound id 0x10021FC..0x1002237 written to the dialogue task. When slot != host+108 and the dispatch succeeded: Dialogue_LoadAndShowText(host+106, the player's saved name (Dialogue_LoadAndShowText entry 0 -> Save_GetPlayerNameOrDefault; '???' before main-scenario progress 2), side) (+0x2344B0), whose a3 writes the side into entries[4] bit 0x100 (message-box tail left/right); then host+108 = slot. Triggers >= 0x1F0 are played immediately.
16.side_effects: latches host+108 = speaker slot; writes the dialogue blip sound id; sets the message-box tail side; may play a voice sfx
16.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x207F70 (switch 0x18..0x1C name remap, side = opcode&1), +0x207370 (+14 side -> portrait slot / flip bit), +0x1D8110 (x -64 vs 464), +0x2344B0 (a3 -> entries[4] bit 0x100); corpus: 19908 uses; player lines use the even (left) op 19,908x vs 28x odd, NPC lines mostly the odd (right) op. 37.details: RF4S.exe+0x207F70: slot = (opcode-16)>>1 = 10, side = opcode & 1 = 1. 111.description: Sets the target of an actor's secondary yaw (a second rotation separate from the body facing that TurnActorToAngle changes); the engine eases towards it. Scenes use it after an emote to make a character glance aside and back (60 then 0). Pair with WaitActorAuxYaw.

115.description: Walk an actor to an absolute tile and face the given direction, then lock the NPC's AI so it holds its staged position. Returns at once; follow with WaitActorMoveDone to wait for arrival.
115.details: NPC: move cmd {byte0 jump, byte1 kind 4, u16 yaw 181*facing, u16 speed ((167773*speed)>>12)*(4096|4915.2)>>12, x<<12, y<<12}; npc+568 bit 0x800000 = jump, npc entry +160 = 2, Npc_StartMoveTowards (+0x225A90), then actor+568 |= 0x10 (AI lock). Player (id 0): same data queued with Scene_QueueGenericMoveCommand(host+872, kind 2) (+0x22FD00), no lock. Coordinates are absolute (no current-position anchor).
115.side_effects: NPC move state, actor+568 bits 0x10 / 0x800000; or a queued player move
115.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x1FB380: `HIDWORD(v32)=dx<<12; v33=dy<<12; LOWORD(v32)=181*facing; ... Npc_StartMoveTowards(id,&cmd); *(u32*)(actor+568) |= 0x10`; corpus 226 uses, all argc 6 (speed 100/200/80, jump 0/1), typically followed by WaitActorMoveDone.

117.description: Walks an NPC to an absolute tile, turning to face the way it walks (no end facing). Does not wait; follow with WaitActorMoveDone.
117.details: Cmd {byte0 = jump, byte1 = 0 (mode 0: face travel, reset to the walk animation), x<<12, y<<12, speed}; after Npc_StartMoveTowards it sets actor+568 |= 0x10 (the scene-controlled bit the dispatcher also sets on all NPCs at scene start). Id 0 is looked up in the NPC slot table like any NPC (no player-mover branch). Move command built for Npc_StartMoveTowards (RF4S.exe+0x225A90): byte0 = jump flag (sets actor+568 bit 0x800000 and npc+20 bit 0x200), byte1 = mode (bit 1 -> actor+568 |= 0x20000 keep facing; bit 2 -> npc+20 |= 0x800 turn to the end angle; bit 3 -> skip Npc_FinalizeTeleportAndNotify, i.e. keep the current animation), target x/y in Q12 (tile << 12), speed word = ((speed*167773)>>12) * (4915.2 if jump else 4096.0) >> 12. The op does not wait; pair it with WaitActorMoveDone.
117.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x1FB670: `v24[0] = jump; v24[1] = 0; v27 = x << 12; v28 = y << 12; Npc_StartMoveTowards(id, v24); *(npc->actor+568) |= 0x10`; corpus: 762 uses, e.g. (tag3, reg0, reg1, 100, 0) then WaitActorMoveDone.

181.blocking: yes: until an event actor with that key exists
181.description: Turn a spawned event actor into a peaceful, talkable NPC-like prop: it stops fighting altogether (no attacks on the player, no retaliation when hit, no attacks on other monsters), keeps its idle animation and stays where it is, and the player can now interact with it. Which scene talking runs is chosen by the actor's EVENT KEY: the type-2 entry with that key in the map's tail bank, then the primary bank, then the global bank (no entry = nothing happens). It is NOT removed, gets no villager features (schedule, gifts, friendship) and does not join the party. The shipped scripts call it right after SpawnEventActor for mounts and extras (e.g. Ventuswill in bank 216 before MountActor). To remove an event actor use KillEventActor or UnregisterEventActor.
181.details: RF4S.exe+0x215100: finds the g_calendarEventMng record by key (returns 1 = the statement waits while none exists); unless actor+16 bit 2 is already set (the reset's own mark, so a second call does nothing) it runs Actor_ResetToTameAndLeaveParty (+0x15B0F0), a general 'tame, not in the party' reset whose party-slot removal only happens when actor+16 bit 0x200 (party member) is set. For every actor it: sets actor+16 bit 2 and clears bits 0x4 (WILD monster: Actor_RecomputeAllStats uses it for the wild model and kill XP; the talk gate in Player_TickFieldInteraction refuses actors with it) and 0x200; rewrites control flags (clears 0x80 / 0x40000, sets 0x100, plus 0x10 | 0x400 for ids < 48); sets the collision volume bytes +0x8A/+0x8B = 4/5 and the attack-info bytes +0x8A/+0x8B = 8/1; recomputes stats (ids < 48 also lose their AI buffers and get full HP). The op then decrements the event manager's companion counter (dword 321, floor 0), sets task work+40 bit 0x40000000 and clears control flag 0x100. Which of these writes stops the attacks exactly was not traced: the monster AI hunts the party only while its AI-context flag 8 is set (Monster_PickClosestVisibleTargetFromParty +0x1C6A70), and no writer of that flag was found in this pass.
181.side_effects: clears the wild-monster bit (the talk gate then lets the player interact; the event key selects the type-2 scene) and resets the hit/collision group bytes; decrements the event manager's companion counter
181.evidence: RF4S.exe+0x215100 and Actor_ResetToTameAndLeaveParty (+0x15B0F0), decompiled 2026-09-28; corpus: 23 uses, every one directly after SpawnEventActor with the actor used afterwards (bank 216 MountActor, bank 215 SetEventActorAlpha, bank 68); checked in game 2026-09-28 by the user: without it a spawned Ventuswill (char 235) attacks the player, with it she stays put, keeps idling, can be hit but never hits back, ignores wild monsters, and can be interacted with. The talk gate in Player_TickFieldInteraction refuses actors with actor+16 bit 0x4, which this op clears; for a registered event actor NpcAi_TickOne goes to NpcAi_ResolveMonsterBehavior (+0x1F9610), which looks up the type-2 entry keyed by the actor's event key (EventActor_GetKeyOfActor +0x1D3540): in the user's test, key 1000 in the Dragon Room tail bank (308) runs @0x748a, key 200 has no entry and nothing happens.
181.notes: Corrected 2026-09-28 twice: it does not remove the actor (the 2026-09-27 review read task bit 0x40000000 as 'dispose'), and it is not limited to party companions — the routine's party removal is conditional; for a non-party monster the effect is losing the wild bit. The old note 'the player cannot be dismissed' rested on actor+16 bit 2, which is the reset's own mark.
181.change_reason: 2026-09-28, user's choice after in-game tests: the op neither dismisses nor removes the actor; it makes it a peaceful, talkable prop. Was DismissEventActor, then briefly DisableEventActorCombat.

0xFFFF.description: Return-or-end -- the VM's real RETURN instruction (IDA-verified: Script_Opcode_FFFF_EndAndCleanup, RF4S.exe+0x23EBA0). Discards the current frame's locals, then: inside a CALLed subroutine it pops the saved PC and resumes right after the CALL; at the top level (frame base 0) it ends the scene (task state 1 READY). So `CALL -> Lx ... Lx: ... RET` is a subroutine, and only a top-level RET terminates the script. (Displayed as END before 2026-09-01.)

0xFFF7.description: Indexed jump table: evaluate the selector expression, then jump to targets[value] when 0 <= value < N -- a DENSE 0..N-1 index, not a set of per-case compare values. The comparison is UNSIGNED, so a negative selector (like reg0 = -1 after a cancelled prompt) falls through to the next statement, same as any >= N value. The canonical use is dispatching a choice result: `SWITCH (reg0)` after a staged PROMPT_CHOICE jumps to the picked option's branch. Layout: [op][selector-expr][N][N u16 targets]. IDA-verified (Script_VMStep case 0xFFF7, RF4S.exe+0x23EF60).
0xFFF7.evidence: Script_VMStep case 0xFFF7: value < N (unsigned) -> pc = targets[value]; else pc += 2*(N+3) (falls through)

0xFFF5.operands: N, N targets, N u32 text ids
0xFFF5.blocking: yes: until an option is picked
0xFFF5.description: Present a choice menu with NO cancel key -- one of the N options must be picked (the cancel key does nothing). Same UI as PROMPT_CHOICE: each option is a full u32 rf3mc.<locale> text id (no flag bits; an id past the archive shows entry 0), 4 rows on screen with a wrap-around scrolling list, at most 128 options (the rest are silently dropped); option text goes through the normal ＠ substitution pass. Branches to targets[picked VISIBLE ROW]. reg0 is written ONLY when a visibility mask is set (ops 610/611/612): then only flagged options appear, reg0 = the picked option's ORIGINAL index, the mask is cleared, and the shipped idiom is all targets -> one label + SWITCH on reg0. A mask whose set bits all lie past option N-1 opens an EMPTY menu that crashes on confirm (divide by zero); an all-zero mask shows every option. An unmasked prompt leaves reg0 UNTOUCHED -- shipped scenes carry a GetPlayerPosition result in reg0/reg1 across a Yes/No prompt (the deck-fight chase). CalcChoicePrescroll (613) sets the initially highlighted row. Layout: [op][N][N u16 targets][N u32 items]; size 6N+4. IDA-verified 2026-09-24 (Script_VMStep case 0xFFF5, SceneEvent_FinalizeAndPickFromBitmap, ChoiceDialog_TickStateMachine).
0xFFF5.evidence: Script_VMStep case 0xFFF5: choice_begin(N, 0); items at pc+2*(N+2)+4*i; pc = targets[pick]

0xFFF2.prototype: JMP_WEIGHTED N, N targets, N weight expressions
0xFFF2.operands: N, N targets, N weight expressions
0xFFF2.description: Weighted-random branch: pick one of N targets at random, each weighted by an expression. Every case's weight is evaluated fresh (so a weight can depend on game state), the weights are summed, then an RNG roll in [0, total) selects a target -- case i fires with probability weight[i] / sum(weights) (weight 0 = never taken). The editable literals on this op ARE those per-target weights, so raising one tilts the odds toward its branch. Layout: [op][N][N u16 targets][N u16 weight-exprs]; size 4N+4. IDA-verified (Script_VMStep case 0xFFF2 -> Script_Opcode_FFF2_ExecPrim, RF4S.exe+0x23EC40).
0xFFF2.evidence: Script_Opcode_FFF2_ExecPrim (RF4S.exe+0x23EC40): sums the N weights, roll in [0, total), walks the cumulative weights; pc = targets[pick]

0xFFF1.description: Frame setup (it does NOT return): sets the frame base to the stack top, reserves N stack words, and falls through. The reserved words are the spill room of the expression evaluator: an expression of depth d writes 2*(d-1) words at the frame base (8-byte {kind, value} slots), and an action pushes its arguments (value, kind) last to first at the stack top = frame base + N. So an action argument that is a nested expression (e.g. reg0 + 1) and not the last one needs N >= 2*(depth-1), or it overwrites the arguments already pushed. Literals, registers and flags (depth 1), branch conditions and EVAL never need it. The shipped scripts never need theirs (FRAME 2 everywhere is compiler slack); the editor adds / raises FRAME by itself when an edit needs it.
0xFFF1.evidence: Script_VMStep case 0xFFF1: frame base = stack top; reserve N words; pc += 4 (falls through). Script_EvalExpressionOrVar passes &stack[frame_base] as the evaluator's spill stack (Script_EvalExpressionBytecode RF4S.exe+0x23E1C0 keeps the top in a local and spills the rest as ScriptStackSlot_t {kind u8 @0, value @4}); Script_PrepActionArgs (+0x23EE10) evaluates args last to first and pushes value then kind at the stack top. Every one of the 38,595 shipped routine entries meets FRAME >= 2*(depth-1) of its non-last action args (33,556 have no FRAME and need none). In-game test 2026-09-29 (user): EVAL (reg0 = 1), EVAL (reg1 = 2), GivePlayerItem((reg0 + (reg1 * 63)), 5, 1) gives 5 Recovery Potions lv 1 with FRAME 4 (Dragon Room) and 8 lv 7 without a FRAME (MAP_FIELD_02): the spilled reg0 / reg1 slots put their kind bytes 7 / 8 where the pushed quality / count values were.
0xFFF1.change_reason: 2026-09-29: the 'reserves slots for locals' reading was wrong -- the words are the evaluator's spill room (verified in game).
